    # Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs
    
    Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.
    
    Start by classifying how much process the request needs, then work
    through your path: understand the context, refine the idea, present a
    design, and get your human partner's approval.
    
    ## Establish Shared Understanding
    
    The outcome of brainstorming is an understanding your human partner can
    recognize and correct, grounded in what they want to accomplish.
    
    1. **Discover intent.** Use the request and available context to identify
       the intended outcome, who it is for, and what success looks like. When
       that information is missing, ask one focused question about purpose or
       intended use before proposing features or an approach. Knowing the app
       genre does not tell you why your partner wants it. Gathering missing
       requirements does not ask them to authorize the task again.
    2. **Write back your understanding.** Summarize the intended outcome,
       relevant constraints, and success criteria in a short note your partner
       can assess. Separate what they said from assumptions. Invite correction
       and incorporate their answer before treating this as the design brief.
    3. **Carry intent into the design.** Preserve the agreed understanding in
       the selected path's design artifact: the written spec for architectural
       work, or the in-chat design/probe for bounded work and spikes. Check
       proposed features and technical choices against that understanding.
    
    When the request already supplies the purpose and constraints, reflect
    that understanding instead of asking the same questions again. Keep the
    note concise; its accuracy and the opportunity to correct it matter.
    
    <HARD-GATE>
    Before taking any implementation action, including invoking an
    implementation skill, writing product code, scaffolding, installing
    product dependencies, or creating an external project, complete the
    selected path's prerequisites:
    
    - Spike: the human partner approves the question and probe.
    - Bounded: the human partner approves the short in-chat design.
    - Architectural: the human partner reviews and approves the written spec,
      then reviews the written implementation plan and selects its execution
      method. Conversational design approval only permits writing the spec;
      written-spec approval only permits invoking writing-plans.
    
    A reply approves the stage actually presented. Approval of an idea or
    feature scope does not approve artifacts that do not exist yet. Resume
    at the earliest incomplete stage; do not turn one approval into permission
    to skip the rest of the selected path. Read-only project exploration is
    allowed while those prerequisites remain incomplete.
    </HARD-GATE>
    
    ## Three Paths
    
    Before your first question, classify the request and say the
    classification out loud â€” "this looks bounded, so I'll present a short
    design here rather than write a spec" â€” so your human partner can
    override it:
    
    - **Spike** â€” a feasibility question ("can we...", "is it possible...",
      "quick and dirty is fine") whose output is an answer, not code you
      keep. Present the question and what you'll try in 2-3 sentences, get
      a nod, then find out as cheaply as correctness allows. No design
      doc, no spec file. Report findings as a recommendation; anything you
      built stays labeled throwaway.
    - **Bounded** â€” a well-scoped change to code that already exists in
      this repo: a new flag, a small endpoint, a one-file fix.
      Understanding the kind of app is not enough â€” bounded means the flow
      you are changing is already here to read. If there is no existing
      flow to change, the task is not bounded. Ask the clarifying
      questions that matter, present a short design IN CHAT (a few
      sentences to a few short paragraphs), and STOP. Implementation
      starts only after your human partner says yes to that design â€” a
      bounded task's approval is as hard a gate as an architectural
      one. No spec file, no implementation plan document.
    - **Architectural** â€” new projects, new subsystems, changes that
      restructure how components fit together or alter interfaces others
      depend on. Follow the full process: questions, approaches, sectioned
      design, written spec, then the writing-plans skill.
    
    When in doubt between two paths, take the heavier one. The ratchet is
    one-way: hidden complexity discovered mid-task upgrades the path â€”
    stop, say so, and step up. Nothing downgrades mid-task.
    
    ## Anti-Pattern: "Too Simple To Need Approval"
    
    Every path ends with your human partner approving the required design
    before implementation. A bounded change may need only two sentences in
    chat. A new todo-list project is architectural and requires the written
    spec and planning handoffs. Scale the artifact to the selected path;
    complete that path's reviews before implementation.
    
    ## Red Flags
    
    | Thought | Reality |
    |---------|---------|
    | "This is too simple to need a design" | Follow the selected path: a bounded change gets a short chat design; an architectural change gets the written spec and planning handoffs. |
    | "I'll call it bounded and skip the spec" | Reaching for a label to skip work IS the doubt â€” take the heavier path. |
    | "It's bounded and the design is obvious â€” I'll start while they read it" | The gate is the approval, not the design's length. Present, then stop until you hear yes. |
    | "I understand this kind of app, so it's bounded" | Bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity. A new project has no existing flow â€” it is architectural. |
    | "The spike works, so I'll keep the code" | A spike's output is an answer. Keeping the code is a new request â€” classify it. |
    | "It grew, but I'm almost done â€” no need to re-classify" | Hidden complexity upgrades the path mid-task. Stop and say so. |
    | "They approved the spike, so the follow-up change is approved too" | Each task gets its own classification and its own approval. |
    
    ## Checklist
    
    Classify first, announce the path, then create a task for each item on
    your path and complete them in order.
    
    **Spike:**
    1. **Explore project context** â€” enough to frame the probe
    2. **Present question + probe plan** â€” 2-3 sentences
    3. **Get approval** â€” a nod is enough
    4. **Investigate** â€” as cheaply as correctness allows
    5. **Report findings** â€” a recommendation; label anything built as throwaway
    
    **Bounded:**
    1. **Explore project context** â€” check files, docs, recent commits
    2. **Ask clarifying questions** â€” one at a time, the ones that matter
    3. **Present short design in chat** â€” approach, files touched, testing
    4. **Get approval** â€” STOP and wait for an explicit yes; presenting the design and starting in the same breath is skipping the gate
    5. **Implement** â€” proceed with the normal development workflow (TDD applies); no plan document
    
    **Architectural:**
    1. **Explore project context** â€” check files, docs, recent commits
    2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** â€” NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
    3. **Ask clarifying questions** â€” one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
    4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** â€” with trade-offs and your recommendation
    5. **Present design** â€” in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
    6. **Write design doc** â€” save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
    7. **Spec self-review** â€” quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
    8. **User reviews written spec** â€” ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
    9. **Transition to implementation** â€” invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan
    
    ## Process Flow
    
    ```dot
    digraph brainstorming {
        "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" [shape=diamond];
        "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [shape=box];
        "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [shape=box];
        "Present short design in chat" [shape=box];
        "Human approves?" [shape=diamond];
        "Investigate; report recommendation" [shape=doublecircle];
        "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [shape=doublecircle];
        "Explore project context" [shape=box];
        "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
        "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
        "Present design sections" [shape=box];
        "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
        "Write design doc" [shape=box];
        "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
        "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
        "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];
        "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" [shape=box];
    
        "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [label="spike"];
        "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [label="bounded"];
        "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Explore project context" [label="architectural"];
        "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" -> "Human approves?";
        "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" -> "Present short design in chat";
        "Present short design in chat" -> "Human approves?";
        "Human approves?" -> "Investigate; report recommendation" [label="spike: yes"];
        "Human approves?" -> "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [label="bounded: yes"];
        "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" -> "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural";
        "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
        "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
        "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
        "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
        "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
        "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
        "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
        "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
        "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
        "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
    }
    ```
    
    **Terminal states are path-bound.** Architectural: the ONLY skill you
    invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans â€” never frontend-design,
    mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. Bounded: after
    approval, implementation proceeds directly through the normal
    development workflow; no plan document. Spike: the terminal state is a
    reported recommendation.
    
    ## The Process
    
    The subsections below serve the bounded and architectural paths (a
    spike stops at "present the probe, get a nod"). Sections from
    **Exploring approaches** onward are architectural-path depth â€” for
    bounded work, context plus a few questions plus a short in-chat design
    is the whole process.
    
    **Understanding the idea:**
    
    - Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
    - Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
    - If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec â†’ plan â†’ implementation cycle.
    - For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
    - Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
    - Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
    - Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria
    
    **Exploring approaches:**
    
    - Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
    - Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
    - Lead with your recommended option and explain why
    - YAGNI ruthlessly - remove unnecessary features from every approach and design
    
    **Presenting the design:**
    
    - Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
    - Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
    - Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
    - Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
    - Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense
    
    **Design for isolation and clarity:**
    
    - Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
    - For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
    - Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
    - Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.
    
    **Working in existing codebases:**
    
    - Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
    - Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
    - Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.
    
    ## After the Design (architectural path)
    
    **Documentation:**
    
    - Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
      - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
    - Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
    - Commit the design document to git
    
    **Spec Self-Review:**
    After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:
    
    1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
    2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
    3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
    4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.
    
    Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review â€” just fix and move on.
    
    **User Review Gate:**
    After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:
    
    > "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."
    
    Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.
    
    **Implementation:**
    
    - Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
    - Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.
    
    ## Visual Companion
    
    A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool â€” not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.
    
    **Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told â€” a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
    > "This next part might be easier if I show you â€” I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."
    
    **This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer â€” no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.
    
    **Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**
    
    - **Use the browser** for content that IS visual â€” mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
    - **Use the terminal** for content that is text â€” requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions
    
    A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question â€” use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question â€” use the browser.
    
    If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
    `skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

    # Using Git Worktrees
    
    ## Overview
    
    Ensure work happens in an isolated workspace. Prefer your platform's native worktree tools. Fall back to manual git worktrees only when no native tool is available.
    
    **Core principle:** Detect existing isolation first. Then use native tools. Then fall back to git. Never fight the harness.
    
    **Announce at start:** "I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace."
    
    ## Step 0: Detect Existing Isolation
    
    **Before creating anything, check if you are already in an isolated workspace.**
    
    ```bash
    GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
    GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
    BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
    ```
    
    **Submodule guard:** `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` is also true inside git submodules. Before concluding "already in a worktree," verify you are not in a submodule:
    
    ```bash
    # If this returns a path, you're in a submodule, not a worktree â€” treat as normal repo
    git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree 2>/dev/null
    ```
    
    **If `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` (and not a submodule):** You are already in a linked worktree. Skip to Step 2 (Project Setup). Do NOT create another worktree.
    
    Report with branch state:
    - On a branch: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` on branch `<name>`."
    - Detached HEAD: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` (detached HEAD, externally managed). Branch creation needed at finish time."
    
    **If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (or in a submodule):** You are in a normal repo checkout.
    
    Has the user already indicated their worktree preference in your instructions? If not, ask for consent before creating a worktree:
    
    > "Would you like me to set up an isolated worktree? It protects your current branch from changes."
    
    Honor any existing declared preference without asking. If the user declines consent, work in place and skip to Step 2.
    
    ## Step 1: Create Isolated Workspace
    
    **You have two mechanisms. Try them in this order.**
    
    ### 1a. Native Worktree Tools (preferred)
    
    The user has asked for an isolated workspace (Step 0 consent). Do you already have a way to create a worktree? It might be a tool with a name like `EnterWorktree`, `WorktreeCreate`, a `/worktree` command, or a `--worktree` flag. If you do, use it and skip to Step 2.
    
    Native tools handle directory placement, branch creation, and cleanup automatically. Using `git worktree add` when you have a native tool creates phantom state your harness can't see or manage.
    
    Only proceed to Step 1b if you have no native worktree tool available.
    
    ### 1b. Git Worktree Fallback
    
    **Only use this if Step 1a does not apply** â€” you have no native worktree tool available. Create a worktree manually using git.
    
    #### Directory Selection
    
    Follow this priority order. Explicit user preference always beats observed filesystem state.
    
    1. **Check your instructions for a declared worktree directory preference.** If the user has already specified one, use it without asking.
    
    2. **Check for an existing project-local worktree directory:**
       ```bash
       ls -d .worktrees 2>/dev/null     # Preferred (hidden)
       ls -d worktrees 2>/dev/null      # Alternative
       ```
       If found, use it. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.
    
    3. **If there is no other guidance available**, default to `.worktrees/` at the project root.
    
    #### Safety Verification (project-local directories only)
    
    **MUST verify directory is ignored before creating worktree:**
    
    ```bash
    git check-ignore -q .worktrees 2>/dev/null || git check-ignore -q worktrees 2>/dev/null
    ```
    
    **If NOT ignored:** Add to .gitignore, commit the change, then proceed.
    
    **Why critical:** Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to repository.
    
    #### Create the Worktree
    
    ```bash
    # Determine path based on chosen location
    path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"
    
    git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
    cd "$path"
    ```
    
    **Sandbox fallback:** If `git worktree add` fails with a permission error (sandbox denial), tell the user the sandbox blocked worktree creation and you're working in the current directory instead. Then run setup and baseline tests in place.
    
    ## Step 2: Project Setup
    
    Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:
    
    ```bash
    # Node.js
    if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi
    
    # Rust
    if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi
    
    # Python
    if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
    if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi
    
    # Go
    if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
    ```
    
    ## Step 3: Verify Clean Baseline
    
    Run tests to ensure workspace starts clean:
    
    ```bash
    # Use project-appropriate command
    npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
    ```
    
    **If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.
    
    **If tests pass:** Report ready.
    
    ### Report
    
    ```
    Worktree ready at <full-path>
    Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
    Ready to implement <feature-name>
    ```
    
    ## Quick Reference
    
    | Situation | Action |
    |-----------|--------|
    | Already in linked worktree | Skip creation (Step 0) |
    | In a submodule | Treat as normal repo (Step 0 guard) |
    | Native worktree tool available | Use it (Step 1a) |
    | No native tool | Git worktree fallback (Step 1b) |
    | `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
    | `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
    | Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
    | Neither exists | Check instruction file, then default `.worktrees/` |
    | Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
    | Permission error on create | Sandbox fallback, work in place |
    | Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
    | No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |
    
    ## Common Rationalizations
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "I'm obviously not in a worktree â€” no need to check" | Run Step 0. Harness-created isolation and submodules both fool eyeballing; the detection commands settle it. |
    | "`git worktree add` is quicker than hunting for a native tool" | A native tool (e.g. `EnterWorktree`) owns placement, branching, and cleanup. Bypassing it is the #1 mistake â€” it creates phantom state your harness can't see or manage. |
    | "The worktree directory is surely ignored already" | Run `git check-ignore`. An unignored worktree directory commits the whole tree into the repo. |
    | "Any directory name works" | Explicit instructions beat an existing project-local directory, which beats the `.worktrees/` default. |
    | "The workspace is fresh â€” baseline tests can wait" | A dirty baseline makes every later failure ambiguous. Run the tests now; proceeding past failures is your human partner's call. |

    description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

    # Test-Driven Development (TDD)
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
    
    **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.
    
    **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
    
    ## When to Use
    
    **Always:**
    - New features
    - Bug fixes
    - Refactoring
    - Behavior changes
    
    **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
    - Throwaway prototypes
    - Generated code
    - Configuration files
    
    Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
    ```
    
    Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.
    
    **No exceptions:**
    - Don't keep it as "reference"
    - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
    - Don't look at it
    - Delete means delete
    
    Implement fresh from tests. Period.
    
    ## Red-Green-Refactor
    
    ```dot
    digraph tdd_cycle {
        rankdir=LR;
        red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
        verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
        green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
        verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
        refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
        next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];
    
        red -> verify_red;
        verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
        verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
        green -> verify_green;
        verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
        verify_green -> green [label="no"];
        refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
        verify_green -> next;
        next -> red;
    }
    ```
    
    ### RED - Write Failing Test
    
    Write one minimal test showing what should happen.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
      let attempts = 0;
      const operation = () => {
        attempts++;
        if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
        return 'success';
      };
    
      const result = await retryOperation(operation);
    
      expect(result).toBe('success');
      expect(attempts).toBe(3);
    });
    ```
    Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    test('retry works', async () => {
      const mock = jest.fn()
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
      await retryOperation(mock);
      expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    });
    ```
    Vague name, tests mock not code
    </Bad>
    
    **Requirements:**
    - One behavior
    - Clear name
    - Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)
    
    ### Verify RED - Watch It Fail
    
    **MANDATORY. Never skip.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test fails (not errors)
    - Failure message is expected
    - Fails because feature missing (not typos)
    
    **Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.
    
    **Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.
    
    ### GREEN - Minimal Code
    
    Write simplest code to pass the test.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        try {
          return await fn();
        } catch (e) {
          if (i === 2) throw e;
        }
      }
      throw new Error('unreachable');
    }
    ```
    Just enough to pass
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(
      fn: () => Promise<T>,
      options?: {
        maxRetries?: number;
        backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
        onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
      }
    ): Promise<T> {
      // YAGNI
    }
    ```
    Over-engineered
    </Bad>
    
    Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.
    
    ### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass
    
    **MANDATORY.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test passes
    - Other tests still pass
    - Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
    
    **Test fails?** Fix code, not test.
    
    **Other tests fail?** Fix now.
    
    **"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
    green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
    the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
    `npm test`, `cargo test` â€” whatever the repo uses) even when your task
    named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
    deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows â€”

    # Messaging Realtime Delivery and Request Loop Design
    
    ## Intended outcome
    
    Admin and rider messages appear in the other participant's open conversation without a manual refresh. Opening a mobile conversation must not start an endless sequence of API requests. Read receipts and unread badges remain accurate, and reconnecting recovers messages missed while disconnected.
    
    This is a repair to the existing admin web and rider mobile messaging feature. The request is to produce a plan; implementation and deployment are subsequent work.
    
    ## Evidence and limits
    
    The current mobile `refreshMessages()` always calls `markConversationRead()`. The server read route emits `conversation-updated` to the reader's user room. The mobile update listener calls `refreshMessages()` again. A controlled in-memory reproduction using the current hook callbacks and route handler produced 11 message GETs and 10 read PUTs from one refresh, with zero message sends; execution was stopped at the eleventh GET.
    
    The message route currently emits `conversation-message` to `conversation_<id>` and the sender's user room. The existing web and mobile clients join their user rooms, but neither requests `join-conversation`. A controlled route reproduction confirmed that a rider reply targets the conversation room and the rider's room, excluding the admin's user room.
    
    `Too many requests. Please try again later.` is the global limiter's error: 1,000 API requests per IP in 15 minutes. The separate message POST limiter returns `Too many messages. Please try again later.` after 30 attempts per authenticated user in 60 seconds. Existing mobile send-cooldown work does not remove the read/update loop.
    
    These findings are based on the current working tree and controlled reproductions. A live admin/mobile verification is still required. The rider API URL is currently `http://192.168.1.19:3001`; the admin development proxy points to `http://127.0.0.1:3001`. Verify that both reach the same backend instance.
    
    ## Selected approach
    
    Use the authenticated user rooms that both clients already join. Resolve authorized conversation participants on the server and emit once to the union of their user rooms. This delivers messages whether a recipient is viewing the conversation or only the inbox and avoids adding a second client room lifecycle.
    
    An alternative is to join and leave authorized conversation rooms on both clients. That adds reconnect, selection, and stale-room cleanup responsibilities and still needs recipient user-room delivery for inbox updates. It is unnecessary for this repair. Periodic polling is also unnecessary because the existing Socket.IO connection supports the required delivery.
    
    ## Global constraints
    
    - Keep the REST routes, message payloads, clientMessageId idempotency, and existing participant permissions unchanged.
    - Keep the global limit at 1,000 API requests per IP per 15 minutes and the message limit at 30 POST attempts per authenticated user per 60 seconds.
    - Emit message content only to authenticated conversation participants who are admins or the currently assigned rider; never broadcast it to admin-room or every connected socket.
    - Persist messages and read state before emitting socket events; a push or realtime delivery failure must not undo a saved message.
    - Do not introduce periodic messaging polling, automatic HTTP 429 retries, new dependencies, database migrations, or unrelated UI, authentication, or location changes.
    - Preserve unrelated working-tree changes and do not commit, publish, or deploy as part of planning.
    
    ## Server event contract
    
    The server adds an internal `listConversationDeliveryTargets(conversationId, actorId)` helper. It first checks the authenticated actor's conversation access, then returns deduplicated `{ userId, requestId }` entries for authorized participants. The SQL must join current user roles and the request's current rider assignment; historical membership alone is insufficient.
    
    After a successful message transaction, broadcast `conversation-message` with the existing `{ conversationId, message }` payload once through `io.to(userIds).emit(...)`. Keep the existing message-related `conversation-updated` payload for compatibility, targeting the same user-room union. Push targets use the same authorized list, excluding the sender.
    
    After a successful read transaction, emit only `conversation-read` with the existing `{ conversationId, userId, readAt }` payload to that union. Stop producing `conversation-updated` for reads. A delivery-target lookup or push failure after persistence is logged without message bodies or tokens and does not turn a saved message into a failed send response. Reconnect synchronization provides recovery when realtime delivery is unavailable.
    
    Existing `join-conversation` authorization can remain for compatibility, but the repaired clients do not rely on conversation-room membership. A previously joined socket must not receive sensitive events merely because it remains in an old conversation room.
    
    ## Mobile behavior
    
    - `conversation-message` upserts the canonical message by server ID and clientMessageId. An incoming message for the focused conversation appears immediately. An own-message echo reconciles the optimistic item without inserting another bubble or sending a read PUT.
    - Only a new message from another participant in the focused conversation triggers a read acknowledgement. Duplicate delivery, unrelated conversations, inactive screens, and own-message echoes do not trigger additional read PUTs.
    - `conversation-read` updates local unread state for the matching reader and requests a bounded inbox/badge reconciliation when necessary. It never reloads message history or sends a read PUT.
    - For compatibility with an older server, a `conversation-updated` payload containing `readAt` is treated as a read receipt. Other updates reconcile inbox metadata and never trigger a full selected-thread reload.
    - Full thread GETs happen on focus, explicit refresh, or recovery of the focused thread after reconnect. Concurrent refresh requests share one in-flight operation. A response for a previously selected conversation cannot replace the current conversation's state.
    - Inbox and badge event refreshes retain a minimum 1,000 ms interval, with one bounded trailing refresh when an event arrives during an in-flight request or that interval. A final event must not be silently lost. Failure clears queued automatic work; HTTP 429 never starts a retry loop.
    - A fetched snapshot merges with canonical messages received while it was in flight and with pending/failed optimistic messages. It does not erase an in-progress send. Respect the existing newest-first mobile ordering and the backend's database timestamp representation.
    - Clean up event listeners and pending refresh timers when the hook is disposed. Reconnect recovery runs only for a focused conversation and once per connection transition, not on every render.
    
    ## Admin behavior
    
    The admin listens to message, read, metadata, and reconnect events. Read receipts clear the reader's matching unread count without invoking `fetchMessages()` or another read PUT. Legacy read-shaped update events follow the same path.
    
    A unique incoming rider message updates the selected thread immediately, acknowledges it once when that conversation is actually visible, and updates the inbox summary. Own-message echoes and duplicate IDs do not increase unread counts or cause repeated read acknowledgements. On narrow screens, a selected ID with the conversation sheet closed is not an actively viewed thread.
    
    Known message-related metadata updates do not cause a second history request. Unknown conversation IDs request one coalesced inbox fetch. Reconnect fetches the inbox and, when visible, the selected thread. In-flight snapshots merge with socket messages and do not replace a newly selected conversation.
    
    ## Scope boundaries
    
    There is no new global message read-marker design. Existing per-participant `last_read_at` remains authoritative for unread counts; a receipt from one admin must not clear another admin's unread count. No changes are required to attachment support, retention, notification presentation, or general location refresh behavior.
    
    ## Acceptance criteria
    
    1. One rider reply and one admin message each reach the other connected participant without manual refresh or conversation-room joins.
    2. Opening a conversation causes a bounded initial fetch/read acknowledgement, then an idle 30-second observation contains zero additional thread GETs, read PUTs, or message POSTs after event work settles.
    3. Read receipts from the current user, another participant, or an unrelated conversation cause zero thread GETs and zero read PUTs.
    4. Duplicate and own-message events do not duplicate bubbles, increment unread counts incorrectly, or repeat read acknowledgements.
    5. Reconnect recovers a message missed offline and retains an optimistic message whose HTTP response has not arrived yet.
    6. Former riders, unrelated users, and personnel sockets do not receive message content through stale membership or broad rooms.
    7. Genuine HTTP 429 responses remain visible without automatic retry storms. A pre-existing limiter window may require waiting for its Retry-After duration after the repair.
    8. Every affected package has fresh lint, typecheck, test, and build evidence in that order. Missing tooling or unrelated failures are reported explicitly and prevent a completion claim.
    
    ## Validation and rollout
    
    Add regression tests that replay captured socket callbacks rather than mocking subscriptions away. Add isolated real-Socket.IO delivery tests with mocked persistence, then a dedicated development-fixture browser/socket check and a physical rider-app check. Measure request counts after settling, not only API message persistence.
    
    Execute the repository quality gate for mobile, web, and server; refresh graphify after code changes. Use existing tools and report the root/server lint-script gap explicitly. Deploy only after the implementation and checks are complete and deployment is separately authorized. Do not reset shared limiter state to hide a regression.

    **Architecture:** Separate new messages, read receipts, and inbox metadata. Route socket events to the union of server-authorized participant user rooms, which the existing clients already join. Make mobile and admin event handling deduplicate messages, acknowledge only visible incoming messages, and reserve full thread fetches for focus, explicit refresh, and reconnect recovery.

    ## Global Constraints
    
    - Keep the REST routes, message payloads, clientMessageId idempotency, and existing participant permissions unchanged.
    - Keep the global limit at 1,000 API requests per IP per 15 minutes and the message limit at 30 POST attempts per authenticated user per 60 seconds.
    - Emit message content only to authenticated conversation participants who are admins or the currently assigned rider; never broadcast it to admin-room or every connected socket.
    - Persist messages and read state before emitting socket events; a push or realtime delivery failure must not undo a saved message.
    - Do not introduce periodic messaging polling, automatic HTTP 429 retries, new dependencies, database migrations, or unrelated UI, authentication, or location changes.
    - Preserve unrelated working-tree changes and do not commit, publish, or deploy as part of planning.
    
    ## Review Focus
    
    - Own-message echoes and duplicate deliveries must reconcile one bubble and cause no repeated read PUTs: Task 1 and Task 3 tests.
    - Receipts for another conversation or another admin must not reload the selected thread or clear the wrong unread count: Task 1 and Task 3 tests.
    - Former riders, changed user roles, and sockets lingering in old rooms must not receive content: Task 2 service/route tests and Task 4 socket tests.
    - Reconnect and an HTTP response racing a new socket message must preserve both canonical and pending messages: Task 1 and Task 3 tests, Task 4 live check.
    - Event bursts, failed requests, and unmount during queued refresh work must stay bounded and stop after HTTP 429: Task 1 scheduler/hook tests and Task 4 request-count checks.

    The previous controlled reproduction yielded 11 message GETs and 10 read PUTs from one mobile refresh, with zero sends. The current server message route targets the conversation room and sender room only. The clients do not request `join-conversation`.

                <span className="shrink-0 text-[11px] font-bold text-slate-400">{formatSummaryDate(conversation.lastMessageAt)}</span>
              </div>
              <div className="mt-1 flex items-center gap-2">
                <span className={cn('shrink-0 text-[10px] font-semibold', online ? 'text-emerald-600' : 'text-slate-400')}>{online ? 'Online' : 'Offline'}</span>
                {conversation.unreadCount > 0 && <Badge className="h-5 min-w-5 justify-center rounded-full bg-primary px-1.5 text-[10px]">{conversation.unreadCount}</Badge>}
              </div>
              <p className="mt-1 truncate text-xs text-slate-500">{conversation.lastMessage?.body || 'No messages yet'}</p>
            </div>
          </div>
        </button>
      );
    }
    
    function ConversationDetail({
      conversation,
      messages,
      loading,
      error,
      draft,
      sending,
      sendError,
      onDraftChange,
      onSend,
      onRetry,
      onBack,
      mobile = false,
      liveMessageIds,
      onBubbleShown,
    }: {
      conversation: ConversationSummary | null;
      messages: ConversationMessage[];
      loading: boolean;
      error: string | null;
      draft: string;
      sending: boolean;
      sendError: string | null;
      onDraftChange: (value: string) => void;
      onSend: () => void;
      onRetry: () => void;
      onBack?: () => void;
      mobile?: boolean;
      liveMessageIds: ReadonlySet<string>;
      onBubbleShown: (id: string) => void;
    }) {
      const messageListRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
      const reducedMotion = useReducedMotion();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        if (messageListRef.current) messageListRef.current.scrollTop = messageListRef.current.scrollHeight;
      }, [messages.length, conversation?.id]);
    
      if (!conversation) {
        return (
          <div className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col items-center justify-center bg-slate-50/60 p-8 text-center">
            <div className="mb-4 flex h-16 w-16 items-center justify-center rounded-2xl bg-white text-slate-300 shadow-sm"><MessageCircle className="h-7 w-7" /></div>
            <h2 className="text-base font-black text-slate-900">Select a conversation</h2>
            <p className="mt-1 max-w-xs text-sm text-slate-500">Choose a request thread to see the riderâ€™s latest updates.</p>
          </div>
        );
      }
    
      return (
        <div className={cn('flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col bg-slate-50/70', mobile && 'h-full')}>
          <div className="shrink-0 border-b border-slate-100 bg-white px-4 py-3 pt-[calc(0.75rem+env(safe-area-inset-top))] md:px-5 md:pt-4">
            <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
              {onBack && <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" onClick={onBack} aria-label="Back to conversations" className="h-10 w-10 shrink-0 rounded-xl"><ArrowLeft className="h-4 w-4" /></Button>}
              <div className="flex h-10 w-10 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-primary text-sm font-black text-white">{conversation.rider.name.slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()}</div>
              <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
                <h2 className="truncate text-sm font-black text-slate-900">{conversation.rider.name}</h2>
                <p className="truncate text-[11px] font-bold uppercase tracking-wider text-slate-400">{requestLabel(conversation)} Â· {conversation.request.deliveryStatus?.replace(/_/g, ' ') || 'Open'}</p>
              </div>
              <Badge variant="outline" className="hidden shrink-0 border-emerald-200 bg-emerald-50 text-[10px] font-black uppercase text-emerald-700 sm:inline-flex">{conversation.status}</Badge>
            </div>
            <div className="mt-3 rounded-xl bg-slate-50 px-3 py-2 text-xs text-slate-600">
              <span className="font-bold">{conversation.request.pickupAddress || 'Pickup not provided'}</span>
              <span className="mx-2 text-slate-300">â†’</span>
              <span>{conversation.request.dropoffAddress || 'Drop-off not provided'}</span>
            </div>
          </div>
    
          <div ref={messageListRef} className="min-h-0 flex-1 space-y-3 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain px-4 py-4 md:px-6" aria-live="polite">
            {loading && messages.length === 0 ? (
              <div className="flex h-full items-center justify-center text-slate-400"><Loader2 className="h-5 w-5 animate-spin" /><span className="sr-only">Loading messages</span></div>
            ) : error ? (
              <div className="m-auto max-w-sm rounded-2xl border border-rose-100 bg-rose-50 p-4 text-center text-sm text-rose-700"><p>{error}</p><Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={onRetry} className="mt-3 rounded-xl border-rose-200 bg-white">Try again</Button></div>
            ) : messages.length === 0 ? (
              <div className="m-auto max-w-sm text-center"><p className="text-sm font-bold text-slate-500">No messages in this thread yet.</p><p className="mt-1 text-xs text-slate-400">Send a quick update to the rider below.</p></div>
            ) : messages.map((message) => {
              const mine = message.sender.role === 'admin';
              return (
                <motion.div key={message.id}
                  initial={liveMessageIds.has(message.id) && !reducedMotion ? { opacity: 0, y: 6, scale: 0.98 } : false}
                  animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, scale: 1 }}
                  transition={{ duration: reducedMotion ? 0 : 0.2, ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] }}
                  onAnimationComplete={() => onBubbleShown(message.id)}
                  className={cn('flex', mine ? 'justify-end' : 'justify-start')}>
                  <div className={cn('max-w-[85%] rounded-2xl px-3.5 py-2.5 shadow-sm sm:max-w-[70%]', mine ? 'rounded-br-md bg-slate-900 text-white' : 'rounded-bl-md border border-slate-100 bg-white text-slate-800')}>
                    <p className="whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-sm leading-relaxed">{message.body}</p>
                    <div className={cn('mt-1.5 flex items-center justify-end gap-1 text-[10px] font-bold', mine ? 'text-slate-400' : 'text-slate-400')}>
                      <span>{formatMessageDate(message.createdAt)}</span>
                      {mine && <span className="relative inline-flex h-3 w-3"><AnimatePresence initial={false}>
                        <motion.span key={message.readAt ? 'read' : 'sent'} className="absolute inset-0 inline-flex"
                          initial={{ opacity: reducedMotion ? 1 : 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
                          transition={{ duration: reducedMotion ? 0 : 0.18 }}>
                          {message.readAt ? <CheckCheck className="h-3 w-3 text-primary" aria-label="Read" /> : <Check className="h-3 w-3" aria-label="Sent" />}
                        </motion.span>
                      </AnimatePresence></span>}
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </motion.div>
              );
            })}
          </div>
    
          <div className="shrink-0 border-t border-slate-100 bg-white px-3 pb-[calc(0.75rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))] pt-3 md:px-5 md:pb-4">
            {sendError && <p className="mb-2 text-xs font-bold text-rose-600" role="alert">{sendError}</p>}
            <div className="flex items-end gap-2">
              <Textarea
                value={draft}
                onChange={(event) => onDraftChange(event.target.value)}
                onKeyDown={(event) => { if (event.key === 'Enter' && !event.shiftKey) { event.preventDefault(); onSend(); } }}
                placeholder="Write an update to the riderâ€¦"
                aria-label="Message to rider"
                disabled={sending || conversation.status !== 'open'}
                className="max-h-32 min-h-11 resize-none rounded-2xl border-slate-200 bg-slate-50 py-3 text-sm focus-visible:ring-primary"
                rows={1}
              />
              <motion.div className="shrink-0" whileTap={{ scale: reducedMotion || sending || !draft.trim() || conversation.status !== 'open' ? 1 : 0.94 }} transition={{ duration: reducedMotion ? 0 : 0.18 }}>
              <Button type="button" onClick={onSend} disabled={sending || !draft.trim() || conversation.status !== 'open'} aria-label="Send message" className="h-11 w-11 shrink-0 rounded-2xl p-0">
                {sending ? <Loader2 className="h-4 w-4 animate-spin" /> : <Send className="h-4 w-4" />}
              </Button>
              </motion.div>
            </div>
            {conversation.status !== 'open' && <p className="mt-2 text-[11px] font-bold text-slate-400">This conversation is closed and read-only.</p>}
          </div>
        </div>
      );
    }
    
    export function AdminMessaging() {
      const { user } = useAuth();
      return <AdminMessagingContent key={user?.id || 'signed-out'} actorId={user?.id || ''} />;
    }
    
    function AdminMessagingContent({ actorId }: { actorId: string }) {
      const { fetchWithAuth, requests } = useData();
      const { socket, riderPresence } = useRealTime();
      const [conversations, setConversations] = useState<ConversationSummary[]>([]);
      const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [messages, setMessages] = useState<ConversationMessage[]>([]);
      const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
      const [messagesLoading, setMessagesLoading] = useState(false);
      const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [messagesError, setMessagesError] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [draft, setDraft] = useState('');
      const [sending, setSending] = useState(false);
      const [sendError, setSendError] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [mobileOpen, setMobileOpen] = useState(false);
      const [startingRequestId, setStartingRequestId] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const isMobile = useIsMobile();
      const reducedMotion = useReducedMotion();
      const viewRef = useRef({ isMobile, mobileOpen, reducedMotion });
      useEffect(() => { viewRef.current = { isMobile, mobileOpen, reducedMotion }; }, [isMobile, mobileOpen, reducedMotion]);
      const [liveMessageIds, setLiveMessageIds] = useState<ReadonlySet<string>>(() => new Set());
      // Each account owns its deduplication and in-flight work. Old callbacks cannot
      // publish into a replacement account or a later selection of the same thread.
      const runtimeRef = useRef({
        disposed: false,
        selectedId: null as string | null,
        selectionVersion: 0,
        conversations: [] as ConversationSummary[],
        threads: new Map<string, ConversationMessage[]>(),
        seen: new Map<string, Set<string>>(),
        counted: new Map<string, Set<string>>(),
        acknowledged: new Set<string>(),
        liveMessageIds: new Set<string>(),
        revision: 0,
        summaryRevisions: new Map<string, number>(),
        inboxPromise: null as Promise<void> | null,
        inboxPending: false,
        threadPromises: new Map<string, { version: number; promise: Promise<void> }>(),
      });
      const isCurrent = useCallback(() => !runtimeRef.current.disposed, []);
      const visibleConversationId = useCallback(() => !viewRef.current.isMobile || viewRef.current.mobileOpen ? runtimeRef.current.selectedId : null, []);
    
      const publishConversations = useCallback((next: ConversationSummary[], changedId: string) => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        runtime.conversations = next;
        runtime.summaryRevisions.set(changedId, ++runtime.revision);
        setConversations(next);
      }, []);
    
      const acknowledge = useCallback(async (conversationId: string, messageKey: string) => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        const key = `${conversationId}:${messageKey}`;
        if (!isCurrent() || visibleConversationId() !== conversationId || runtime.acknowledged.has(key)) return;
        runtime.acknowledged.add(key);
        const version = runtime.selectionVersion;
        try {
          const response = await fetchWithAuth(`/api/conversations/${encodeURIComponent(conversationId)}/read`, { method: 'PUT' });
          if (!response?.ok) await getErrorMessage(response, 'Unable to mark conversation read.');
          if (!isCurrent() || visibleConversationId() !== conversationId || runtime.selectionVersion !== version) return;
          publishConversations(applyConversationRead(runtime.conversations, { conversationId, userId: actorId, readAt: '' }, actorId), conversationId);
        } catch (caught) {
          runtime.acknowledged.delete(key);
          if (isCurrent() && runtime.selectedId === conversationId && runtime.selectionVersion === version) setMessagesError(caught instanceof Error ? caught.message : 'Unable to mark conversation read.');
        }
      }, [actorId, fetchWithAuth, isCurrent, publishConversations, visibleConversationId]);
    
      const selectedConversation = useMemo(() => conversations.find((conversation) => conversation.id === selectedId) || null, [conversations, selectedId]);
    
      const fetchConversations = useCallback(function refreshInbox(trailing = false): Promise<void> {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        if (!isCurrent()) return Promise.resolve();
        if (runtime.inboxPromise) {
          if (trailing) runtime.inboxPending = true;
          return runtime.inboxPromise;
        }
        const startedRevision = runtime.revision;
        let succeeded = false;
        const promise = (async () => {
          try {
            const response = await fetchWithAuth('/api/conversations?limit=50');
            if (!response?.ok) await getErrorMessage(response, 'Unable to load conversations.');
            const data = await response!.json() as { conversations?: ConversationSummary[] };
            if (!isCurrent()) return;
            const changed = runtime.conversations.filter(item => (runtime.summaryRevisions.get(item.id) || 0) > startedRevision);
            const changedIds = new Set(changed.map(item => item.id));
            const fetched = (data.conversations || []).filter(item => !changedIds.has(item.id));
            runtime.conversations = [...changed, ...fetched];
            fetched.forEach(item => { if (item.lastMessage) recordAdminMessage(runtime.counted, item.lastMessage); });
            setConversations(runtime.conversations);
            setError(null);
            succeeded = true;
          } catch (caught) {
            if (isCurrent()) setError(caught instanceof Error ? caught.message : 'Unable to load conversations.');
          } finally {
            runtime.inboxPromise = null;
            const pending = runtime.inboxPending;
            runtime.inboxPending = false;
            if (isCurrent()) {
              setLoading(false);
              if (succeeded && pending) void refreshInbox();
            }
          }
        })();
        runtime.inboxPromise = promise;
        return promise;
      }, [fetchWithAuth, isCurrent]);
    
      const fetchMessages = useCallback((conversationId: string): Promise<void> => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        if (!isCurrent() || runtime.selectedId !== conversationId) return Promise.resolve();
        const version = runtime.selectionVersion;
        const existing = runtime.threadPromises.get(conversationId);
        if (existing?.version === version) return existing.promise;
        const currentSelection = () => isCurrent() && runtime.selectedId === conversationId && runtime.selectionVersion === version;
        runtime.liveMessageIds.clear();
        const promise = (async () => {
          try {
            const response = await fetchWithAuth(`/api/conversations/${encodeURIComponent(conversationId)}/messages?limit=100`);
            if (!response?.ok) await getErrorMessage(response, 'Unable to load messages.');
            const data = await response!.json() as MessagePage;
            if (!currentSelection()) return;
            const fetched = (data.messages || []).slice().reverse();
            const merged = mergeFetchedAdminMessages(runtime.threads.get(conversationId) || [], fetched);
            fetched.forEach(message => { recordAdminMessage(runtime.seen, message); recordAdminMessage(runtime.counted, message); });
            runtime.threads.set(conversationId, merged);
            setMessagesError(null);
            setLiveMessageIds(new Set(runtime.liveMessageIds));
            setMessages(merged);
            const incoming = [...merged].reverse().find(message => message.sender.id !== actorId);
            if (incoming) void acknowledge(conversationId, `${incoming.sender.id}:${incoming.clientMessageId || incoming.id}`);
          } catch (caught) {
            if (currentSelection()) setMessagesError(caught instanceof Error ? caught.message : 'Unable to load messages.');
          } finally {
            if (runtime.threadPromises.get(conversationId)?.version === version) runtime.threadPromises.delete(conversationId);
            if (currentSelection()) setMessagesLoading(false);
          }
        })();
        runtime.threadPromises.set(conversationId, { version, promise });
        return promise;
      }, [acknowledge, actorId, fetchWithAuth, isCurrent]);
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        runtime.disposed = false;
        void fetchConversations();
        return () => { runtime.disposed = true; runtime.inboxPending = false; };
      }, [fetchConversations]);
    
      useEffect(() => {
        if (selectedId && (!isMobile || mobileOpen)) void fetchMessages(selectedId);
      }, [selectedId, isMobile, mobileOpen, fetchMessages]);
    
      const upsertMessage = useCallback((message: ConversationMessage, animate: boolean) => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        const current = runtime.threads.get(message.conversationId) || [];
        const next = mergeFetchedAdminMessages([message], current);
        runtime.threads.set(message.conversationId, next);
        if (runtime.selectedId === message.conversationId) {
          if (animate && visibleConversationId() === message.conversationId && !viewRef.current.reducedMotion) {
            runtime.liveMessageIds.add(message.id);
            setLiveMessageIds(new Set(runtime.liveMessageIds));
          }
          setMessages(next);
        }
      }, [visibleConversationId]);
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        if (!socket || !actorId) return;
        const handleMessage = (payload: ConversationMessageEvent) => {
          if (!isCurrent() || payload.conversationId !== payload.message.conversationId) return;
          const received = receiveAdminMessage(runtime.conversations, payload.message, visibleConversationId(), actorId, runtime.seen, runtime.counted);
          upsertMessage(payload.message, received.unique);
          const known = runtime.conversations.find(item => item.id === payload.conversationId);
          if (!known) void fetchConversations(true);
          else if (received.unique) publishConversations(received.conversations, known.id);
          if (received.shouldAcknowledge) {
            void acknowledge(payload.conversationId, `${payload.message.sender.id}:${payload.message.clientMessageId || payload.message.id}`);
          }
        };
        const cleanup = subscribeAdminMessaging(socket, {
          onMessage: handleMessage,
          onRead: (payload: ConversationReadEvent) => {
            if (isCurrent() && payload.userId === actorId) publishConversations(applyConversationRead(runtime.conversations, payload, actorId), payload.conversationId);
          },
          onMetadata: payload => {
            if (!isCurrent()) return;
            const known = runtime.conversations.find(item => item.id === payload.conversationId);
            if (!known) { void fetchConversations(true); return; }
            if (payload.lastMessage?.conversationId === payload.conversationId) {
              const next = mergeConversationMessage(runtime.conversations, payload.lastMessage, payload.conversationId, actorId);
              publishConversations(next.map(item => item.id === known.id ? { ...item, unreadCount: known.unreadCount } : item), known.id);
            }
          },
          onConnect: () => {
            if (!isCurrent()) return;
            void fetchConversations(true);
            const visible = visibleConversationId();
            if (visible) void fetchMessages(visible);
          },
        });
        return () => {
          cleanup();
          runtime.inboxPending = false;
        };
      }, [acknowledge, actorId, fetchConversations, fetchMessages, isCurrent, publishConversations, socket, upsertMessage, visibleConversationId]);
    
      const selectConversation = (conversationId: string) => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        if (runtime.selectedId !== conversationId || (viewRef.current.isMobile && !viewRef.current.mobileOpen)) setMessagesLoading(true);
        if (runtime.selectedId !== conversationId) {
          runtime.selectedId = conversationId;
          runtime.selectionVersion++;
          runtime.liveMessageIds.clear();
          setLiveMessageIds(new Set());
          setMessages(runtime.threads.get(conversationId) || []);
          setMessagesError(null);
          setDraft('');
          setSendError(null);
        }
        viewRef.current.mobileOpen = true;
        setSelectedId(conversationId);
        setMobileOpen(true);
      };
    
      const startConversation = async (requestId: string) => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        if (startingRequestId) return;
        setStartingRequestId(requestId);
        setError(null);
        try {
          const response = await fetchWithAuth('/api/conversations', {
            method: 'POST',
            body: JSON.stringify({ requestId }),
          });
          if (!response?.ok) await getErrorMessage(response, 'Unable to start conversation.');
          const conversation = await response!.json() as ConversationSummary;
          if (!isCurrent()) return;
          publishConversations([conversation, ...runtime.conversations.filter((item) => item.id !== conversation.id)], conversation.id);
          selectConversation(conversation.id);
        } catch (caught) {
          if (isCurrent()) setError(caught instanceof Error ? caught.message : 'Unable to start conversation.');
        } finally {
          if (isCurrent()) setStartingRequestId(null);
        }
      };
    
      const sendMessage = async () => {
        const runtime = runtimeRef.current;
        if (!selectedConversation || !draft.trim() || sending) return;
        const body = draft.trim();
        const conversationId = selectedConversation.id;
        const version = runtime.selectionVersion;
        setSending(true);
        setSendError(null);
        try {
          const response = await fetchWithAuth(`/api/conversations/${encodeURIComponent(selectedConversation.id)}/messages`, {
            method: 'POST',
            body: JSON.stringify({ clientMessageId: globalThis.crypto.randomUUID(), body }),
          });
          if (!response?.ok) await getErrorMessage(response, 'Unable to send message.');
          const message = await response!.json() as ConversationMessage;
          if (!isCurrent()) return;
          const unique = recordAdminMessage(runtime.seen, message);
          upsertMessage(message, unique);
          if (unique) publishConversations(mergeConversationMessage(runtime.conversations, message, visibleConversationId(), actorId), conversationId);
          if (runtime.selectedId === conversationId && runtime.selectionVersion === version) setDraft('');
        } catch (caught) {
          if (isCurrent() && runtime.selectedId === conversationId && runtime.selectionVersion === version) setSendError(caught instanceof Error ? caught.message : 'Unable to send message.');
        } finally {
          if (isCurrent()) setSending(false);
        }
      };
    
      const detailProps = {
        conversation: selectedConversation,
        messages,
        loading: messagesLoading,
        error: messagesError,
        draft,
        sending,
        sendError,
        onDraftChange: setDraft,
        onSend: sendMessage,
        onRetry: () => {
          if (selectedId) { setMessagesError(null); setMessagesLoading(true); void fetchMessages(selectedId); }
        },
        liveMessageIds,
        onBubbleShown: (id: string) => {
          if (runtimeRef.current.liveMessageIds.delete(id)) setLiveMessageIds(new Set(runtimeRef.current.liveMessageIds));
        },
      };
    
      return (
        <div className="flex h-full min-h-0 flex-col bg-white">
          <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center justify-between border-b border-slate-100 bg-white px-4 py-4 md:px-6">
            <div><p className="text-[10px] font-black uppercase tracking-[0.22em] text-primary">Operations</p><h1 className="mt-1 text-xl font-black tracking-tight text-slate-900">Inbox</h1></div>
            <div className="flex items-center gap-2"><Badge variant="outline" className="rounded-full border-primary/20 bg-primary/5 text-primary"><Inbox className="mr-1.5 h-3.5 w-3.5" />{totalUnreadConversations(conversations)} unread</Badge><Button variant="ghost" size="icon" onClick={() => void fetchConversations()} aria-label="Refresh inbox" className="h-10 w-10 rounded-xl"><RefreshCw className="h-4 w-4" /></Button></div>
          </div>
          <div className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-hidden">
            <aside className="flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col overflow-hidden border-r border-slate-100 md:w-[min(24rem,38%)] lg:w-[22rem]">

      async function client(userId: string, overlap = false): Promise<Client> {
        const socket = connect(url, { auth: { userId, overlap }, transports: ['websocket'],
          autoConnect: false, reconnection: false, forceNew: true });
        const recorded: Client = { socket, events: [] };
        clients.push(recorded);
        socket.onAny((event, payload) => {
          if (['conversation-message', 'conversation-updated', 'conversation-read'].includes(event)) {
            recorded.events.push({ event, payload });
          }
        });
        socket.on('barrier', (_nonce, acknowledge) => acknowledge());
        await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
          const timer = setTimeout(() => { cleanup(); reject(new Error('Socket connection timeout')); }, 3000);
          const cleanup = () => { clearTimeout(timer); socket.off('connect', onConnect); socket.off('connect_error', onError); };
          const onConnect = () => { cleanup(); resolve(); };
          const onError = (error: Error) => { cleanup(); reject(error); };
          socket.once('connect', onConnect);
          socket.once('connect_error', onError);
          socket.connect();
        });
        await socket.timeout(3000).emitWithAck('ready');
        return recorded;
      }
    
      // Ordered server-to-client ACKs ensure forbidden late packets cannot pass
      // an absence assertion just because the network has not flushed yet.

        await io.timeout(3000).emitWithAck('barrier', randomUUID());
      }

    ---
    name: systematic-debugging
    description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
    ---
    
    # Systematic Debugging
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
    
    **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
    ```
    
    If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    Use for ANY technical issue:
    - Test failures
    - Bugs in production
    - Unexpected behavior
    - Performance problems
    - Build failures
    - Integration issues
    
    **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
    - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
    - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
    - You've already tried multiple fixes
    - Previous fix didn't work
    - You don't fully understand the issue
    
    **Don't skip when:**
    - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
    - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
    - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
    
    ## The Four Phases
    
    You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
    
    ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
    
    **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
    
    1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
       - Don't skip past errors or warnings
       - They often contain the exact solution
       - Read stack traces completely
       - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
    
    2. **Reproduce Consistently**
       - Can you trigger it reliably?
       - What are the exact steps?
       - Does it happen every time?
       - If not reproducible â†’ gather more data, don't guess
    
    3. **Check Recent Changes**
       - What changed that could cause this?
       - Git diff, recent commits
       - New dependencies, config changes
       - Environmental differences
    
    4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
    
       **WHEN system has multiple components (CI â†’ build â†’ signing, API â†’ service â†’ database):**
    
       **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
       ```
       For EACH component boundary:
         - Log what data enters component
         - Log what data exits component
         - Verify environment/config propagation
         - Check state at each layer
    
       Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
       THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
       THEN investigate that specific component
       ```
    
       **Example (multi-layer system):**

       # Layer 1: Workflow
       echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
       echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

       security list-keychains

    +  conversation: ConversationSummary; rider: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof login>>;
    +}) => Promise<void>) {

    +  const rider = await login(RIDER.email, RIDER.password!);

    +  const riderApi = await playwrightRequest.newContext({ extraHTTPHeaders: { Authorization: `Bearer ${rider.token}` } });
    +  try {
    +    const response = await adminApi.get(`${API_BASE_URL}/requests?limit=100`);

    +    expect(assigned, 'Dedicated rider must have an assigned request').toBeTruthy();
    +    const result = await adminApi.get(`${API_BASE_URL}/requests/${assigned.request_id}/conversation`);
    +    expect(result.ok()).toBeTruthy();
    +    const conversation = await result.json() as ConversationSummary;

    +    await adminApi.dispose();
    +    await riderApi.dispose();
    +  }
    +}
    +
    +function monitor(page: Page, conversationId: string) {
    +  const calls: string[] = [];
    +  const limited: string[] = [];
    +  const receipts: string[] = [];
    +  page.on('request', request => {
    +    const path = new URL(request.url()).pathname;
    +    if (path === `/api/conversations/${conversationId}/messages` || path === `/api/conversations/${conversationId}/read`) {
    +      calls.push(`${request.method()} ${path}`);
    +    }
    +  });
    +  page.on('response', response => {
    +    if (response.status() === 429 && new URL(response.url()).pathname.startsWith('/api/')) limited.push(response.url());
    +  });
    +  page.on('websocket', socket => socket.on('framereceived', ({ payload }) => {
    +    const packet = String(payload);
    +    if (packet.includes('conversation-read')) receipts.push(packet);
    +  }));
    +  return { calls, limited, receipts };
    +}
    +
    +async function openInbox(page: Page, conversation: ConversationSummary, narrow = false) {
    +  await page.goto('/');
    +  await page.getByLabel('Email address', { exact: true }).fill(ADMIN.email);
    +  await page.locator('#login-password').fill(ADMIN.password);
    +  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign In', exact: true }).click();
    +  if (narrow) await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open admin navigation' }).click();
    +  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Inbox', exact: true }).click();
    +  await page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Inbox', exact: true }).waitFor();
    +  // The summary body uniquely identifies the dedicated fixture, even with several threads for one rider.
    +  await page.getByRole('button').filter({ has: page.getByText(conversation.lastMessage!.body, { exact: true }) }).click();
    +  await page.getByLabel('Message to rider').waitFor();
    +}
    +
    +async function sendRider(riderApi: APIRequestContext, conversationId: string, body: string) {
    +  const response = await riderApi.post(`${API_BASE_URL}/conversations/${conversationId}/messages`, {
    +    data: { clientMessageId: crypto.randomUUID(), body },
    +  });
    +  expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
    +  return await response.json() as ConversationMessage;
    +}
